title: Copilot Studio: labelled and encrypted file uploads for agents on the Microsoft 365 channel
summary: Hold: the billing paragraph presents 2 Copilot Credits as the cost of a generative answer without the additional reasoning-model charge now documented by Microsoft. The roadmap facts and existing controls are supported; two navigation paths need minor completion, and the licensed-user billing statement needs the documented harness qualification.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans support for uploading files protected by Microsoft Purview Information Protection sensitivity labels.
claims.quote: Unblock users from upload files with Microsoft Purview Information Protection (MPIP) sensitivity labels

claims.claim: Learn has not documented the planned labelled-upload feature's detailed behaviour as of November 2026.

claims.quote: Files with encryption, such as sensitivity labels or password protection, aren't supported.

claims.claim: For an encrypted or password-protected Office upload, the agent tells the user that it cannot read the file.
claims.quote: When a user uploads a password-protected or encrypted Office file, the agent tells the user that the file is encrypted or password-protected and can't be read.

claims.claim: Some rights-managed or label-encrypted uploads return a generic error.
claims.quote: For some rights-managed or label-encrypted files, the agent returns a generic error instead.

claims.claim: The file-input page describes agents powered by the standard harness.
claims.quote: This article describes features used in agents or agent flows powered by the standard harness.

claims.claim: The file-input page directs readers to Microsoft Copilot Chat as an experience supporting sensitivity-labelled files.
claims.quote: or use a Microsoft 365 experience such as Microsoft Copilot Chat, which supports sensitivity-labeled files.

claims.claim: Connecting an agent to the Microsoft 365 and Microsoft Teams channels lets users chat with it in Teams and Microsoft Copilot.
claims.quote: After you publish your agent at least once, you can connect it to the Microsoft 365 and Microsoft Teams channels so users can chat with it in both Teams and Microsoft Copilot.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: For the documented general Copilot protection model, EXTRACT determines whether encrypted text can be returned to the user.
claims.quote: The usage right that grants permission to copy text is EXTRACT ... It's this usage right that determines whether Copilot or agents can display text to the user from encrypted content.

claims.claim: The documented encrypted-content model requires VIEW in addition to EXTRACT.
claims.quote: When the sensitivity label applies encryption, users must have the EXTRACT usage right, as well as VIEW, for the AI apps to return the data.

claims.claim: The Purview Copilot Studio page says encryption is supported only with sensitivity labels and only for the SharePoint knowledge source.
claims.quote: Encryption is supported only with sensitivity labels, and only for the SharePoint knowledge source.

claims.claim: The SharePoint troubleshooting page gives a different account, stating that encrypted files cannot be extracted or grounded on.
claims.quote: However, the agent can't extract or ground on content whose protection encrypts the file. This limitation includes sensitivity labels that apply encryption, Double Key Encryption (DKE), and password-protected files.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; controls[3].note
claims.claim: The person applying encryption is the Rights Management owner and retains EXTRACT regardless of the template's restrictions for others.
claims.quote: The person applying the encryption always has the EXTRACT usage right, because they are the Rights Management owner. This special role automatically includes all usage rights and some other actions

claims.claim: Full control (OWNER) includes EXTRACT.
claims.quote: Because the Full control (OWNER) usage right includes all the usage rights, EXTRACT is automatically included with Full control.

claims.claim: The Purview label-encryption path starts at Solutions > Information Protection > Sensitivity labels and reaches Access control through Edit label, the file scope and Control access.
claims.quote: make sure the Files & other data assets option is selected ... on the Choose protection settings for the types of items you selected page ... select Control access. ... On the Access control page
claims.fix: Keep the existing path, whose entry steps are supported by the already-cited https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/create-sensitivity-labels. Append ' > Configure access control settings > Assign permissions now > Assign permissions > users or groups > Choose permissions' to reach the rights selector documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/encryption-sensitivity-labels.

claims.claim: On Access control, Configure access control settings and Assign permissions now are the options used to configure administrator-defined encryption permissions.
claims.quote: When you select Configure access control settings on the Access control page to create or edit a sensitivity label, choose ... Assign permissions now, so that you can determine exactly which users get which permissions

claims.claim: The Purview UI displays EXTRACT as Copy and extract content(EXTRACT).
claims.quote: In the Microsoft Purview portal, the EXTRACT usage right is displayed as Copy and extract content(EXTRACT).

claims.claim: Set-Label -Identity <label> -EncryptionEnabled $true -EncryptionProtectionType Template -EncryptionRightsDefinitions <rights> sets template-based encryption and assigned rights.
claims.quote: The EncryptionRightsDefinitions parameter specifies the rights users have ... This parameter is meaningful only when the EncryptionEnabled parameter value is either $true or $false and the EncryptionProtectionType parameter value is Template.

claims.claim: Copilot and agents generally cannot access unopened SharePoint and OneDrive documents encrypted with user-defined label permissions.
claims.quote: Copilot and agents can't access unopened documents in SharePoint and OneDrive when they're labeled and encrypted with user-defined permissions

claims.claim: A default sensitivity label extending SharePoint permissions to downloaded documents is an exception to the unopened-file restriction.
claims.quote: unless the label is used as a default sensitivity label that extends SharePoint permissions to downloaded documents

claims.claim: Directly referencing a document by typing '/' is the other documented exception.
claims.quote: or they're directly referenced by typing "/"

claims.claim: Both exceptions still require the user's EXTRACT permission.
claims.quote: (and in both cases, the user has EXTRACT permissions).

claims.where: controls[2].note; Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Label-based Copilot DLP is documented for Copilot Studio agents when the knowledge source is SharePoint.
claims.quote: When the knowledge source is SharePoint, a DLP policy scoped to the Microsoft 365 Copilot location can restrict agents built in Copilot Studio for Microsoft Teams, SharePoint, and Microsoft 365 Copilot from processing sensitive content based on a specified sensitivity label.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance controls
claims.claim: DLP does not scan the contents of files uploaded directly into Microsoft 365 Copilot prompts.
claims.quote: DLP can't scan the contents of files that you upload directly into prompts, so evaluation of the uploaded file for sensitive data doesn't occur. DLP only checks the text you type into the prompt itself.

claims.where: controls[2].note; Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not confirmed label-based DLP coverage for the planned agent-upload feature.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio labelled encrypted file uploads Microsoft Purview 571305 File uploads EXTRACT switch API; Copilot Studio pass uploaded files connectors sensitivity labels encryption EXTRACT checks. Opened ai-copilot-studio and Copilot DLP location page; no planned-upload coverage is stated.

claims.claim: The custom DLP policy path reaches the Microsoft Copilot, Copilot Chat, and Copilot Cowork location.
claims.quote: Go to Data Loss Prevention > Policies and select + Create policy. ... Select the Custom template, then Custom policy. ... On the Locations page, set the Microsoft Copilot, Copilot Chat, and Copilot Cowork location to on.
claims.fix: Keep the existing path and add to controls[2].note: 'Add a rule with Content contains > Sensitivity labels and the Prevent Copilot and Cowork from processing content action.' These remaining settings are documented in the cited page's Supported conditions and actions table.

claims.claim: The printed New-DLPCompliancePolicy and New-DLPComplianceRule commands create the label-based Copilot content-processing restriction, with $loc and $advrule defined first.
claims.quote: New-DLPCompliancePolicy -Name "Copilot Policy" -Locations $loc -EnforcementPlanes @("CopilotExperiences") ... New-DLPComplianceRule -Name "Copilot Rule" -Policy "Copilot Policy" -AdvancedRule $advrule -RestrictAccess @(@{setting="ExcludeContentProcessing";value="Block"})

claims.claim: Content contains > Sensitivity labels is the rule condition for excluding labelled items from processing.
claims.quote: Content contains > Sensitivity labels | Prevent Copilot and Cowork from processing content | Detects when a file or an email in Exchange has a chosen sensitivity label.

claims.claim: Purview Data Security AI Admin is among the roles allowed to create or edit policies for this Copilot DLP location.
claims.quote: Accounts with one of the following roles or role groups can create or edit a DLP policy ... Purview Data Security AI Admin - Role for editing Data Loss Prevention policies related to Copilot

claims.claim: Purview recommends enabling sensitivity labels for SharePoint and OneDrive.
claims.quote: If you haven't already, we recommend you enable sensitivity labels for SharePoint and OneDrive and also familiarize yourself with the file types and label configurations that these services can process.

claims.claim: Without SharePoint and OneDrive label enablement, accessible encrypted files are limited to data in use from Office apps on Windows.
claims.quote: When sensitivity labels aren't enabled for these services, the encrypted files that Copilot and agents can access are limited to data in use from Office apps on Windows.

claims.claim: SharePoint and OneDrive sensitivity labels can be enabled at Purview > Solutions > Information Protection > Sensitivity labels > Turn on now.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Information Protection > Sensitivity labels. ... If you see a message to turn on the ability to process content in Office online files, select Turn on now

claims.claim: Set-SPOTenant -EnableAIPIntegration $true enables sensitivity-label support for SharePoint and OneDrive.
claims.quote: To enable the new capabilities, use the Set-SPOTenant cmdlet with the EnableAIPIntegration parameter: ... Set-SPOTenant -EnableAIPIntegration $true

claims.claim: Multi-Geo tenants must use PowerShell to enable this support across geo-locations.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model and notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The existing entitlement model combines Copilot Studio consumption with qualifying Microsoft 365 Copilot licence inclusions, represented as mixed.
claims.quote: Copilot Credits are the common currency across Copilot Studio capabilities. ... If you have a Microsoft 365 Copilot license, using agents in Copilot Chat, Microsoft Teams, or SharePoint for classic answers, generative answers, or Microsoft Graph tenant grounding isn't charged

claims.where: Cost and licensing; front matter: licensing.notes; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Copilot Credits measure agent effort retrieving information, responding to prompts and using actions.
claims.quote: Copilot Credits measure the time and effort your agent needs to retrieve information, respond to prompts, and use any actions or custom Azure Bot Service skills.

claims.claim: A generative answer costs 2 Copilot Credits, subject to the documented Microsoft 365 Copilot-licensed, authenticated employee-facing usage inclusion.
claims.quote: When an agent uses a reasoning-capable language model, Copilot Studio bills by using two billing meters: feature rate and text and generative AI tools (premium). ... Total cost = feature rate for generative answers + text and generative AI tools (premium) per 1000 tokens.
claims.fix: Replace 'A generative answer costs 2 Copilot Credits, subject to the documented Microsoft 365 Copilot-licensed, authenticated employee-facing usage inclusion.' with 'The base feature rate for a generative answer is 2 Copilot Credits. With a reasoning model, the Text and generative AI tools (premium) meter adds 10 Copilot Credits per 1,000 billed tokens, subject to the documented Microsoft 365 Copilot-licensed, authenticated employee-facing usage inclusion.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-copilot-studio/requirements-messages-management.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing: second paragraph; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Classic answers, generative answers and Microsoft Graph tenant grounding in Copilot Chat, Teams or SharePoint are not charged for authenticated Microsoft 365 Copilot-licensed users.
claims.quote: If you have a Microsoft 365 Copilot license, using agents in Copilot Chat, Microsoft Teams, or SharePoint for classic answers, generative answers, or Microsoft Graph tenant grounding isn't charged when the agent runs with your authenticated identity.
claims.fix: Add to the licensing notes and the corresponding Cost and licensing paragraph: 'This inclusion is for employee-facing usage of standard-harness agents and is subject to fair usage limits; the billing-rates page states that it does not apply to agents powered by the Microsoft Copilot harness.' Both pages are already cited; the qualification is in footnote 1 at https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-copilot-studio/requirements-messages-management.
